newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU SEES FINNISH TRADE SURPLUS IN COMING YEARS.
newsitem.headline: EU SEES FINNISH TRADE SURPLUS IN COMING YEARS.

text.p: The Finnish trade and current accounts are expected to continue to show surpluses in the coming years, the European Commission said on Thursday in its 1997 annual economic report.

The report, which did not give any new forecasts, said exports were expected to rebound in 1997 but that due to an increase in imports of consumer durables and investment goods, import growth would exceed that of exports.

"Despite these developments, and as the trade balance surplus is still very large, the trade and current accounts are likely to continue to post surpluses in the coming years," it said in the section about Finland.
The report used the same figures as in the Commission's economic forecast published last November. The next forecast is expected in April.

Turning to inflation, it said that although the price reducing impact of Finland's accession to the European Union was gradually fading out of the consumer price index, "inflation has been, and is expected to remain, subdued."
"The low inflation is supported by wage moderation and moderate import prices," it said.
The report also noted that the Finnish ERM entry had been well received in the market.
